key_insight: A control- and game-theory grounded computational framework models the mutual (co-adaptive) dynamics of users and decoders in closed‑loop neural interfaces, enabling principled design choices that improve stability, learning speed, and personalization.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of principled, predictive models for mutual adaptation in closed‑loop brain–machine interfaces where ad hoc decoder updates and user learning produce unpredictable performance and poor personalization.
method: Formulate user and decoder as interacting agents in a dynamic game / control framework with explicit update rules and objective functions.
Analyze equilibria, stability, and transient behavior to derive design principles (e.g., learning-rate tradeoffs, shaping interventions).
Validate with simulations and closed‑loop experiments to show improved convergence, robustness, and individualized performance through targeted decoder shaping.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a principled toolset to design and tune adaptive human–machine systems with performance guarantees and better user experience, applicable beyond neural interfaces to broader human‑in‑the‑loop ML.
visual_elements: Closed‑loop schematic showing bidirectional interaction: human (intent/learning) ↔ decoder (update rule/controller).
Phase‑space or trajectory plots illustrating convergence vs oscillation under different adaptation settings (stability visual).
Heatmap or contour plot of performance versus user and decoder learning rates to show tradeoffs and design regions.
Timeline or before/after panel showing improvement in task accuracy and personalization when using the proposed shaping strategy.
paper_title: Computational framework to predict and shape human–machine interactions in closed-loop, co-adaptive neural interfaces
paper_authors: Maneeshika M. Madduri, Momona Yamagami, Si Jia Li, Sasha Burckhardt, Samuel A. Burden
